trigger: Resource Ledger for the C++ diff (round 1 and Gate 8 passes 1 and 2)
classification_rationale: informational attestation, not a defect
summary: Resource Ledger: the range adds no owning raw resource (no fd, HANDLE, socket, FILE*, sqlite handle, OpenSSL or BCrypt object, thread, subprocess or temp path). The only lifetime-bearing items are borrowed const ForensicsPluginSet pointers (the set is a ServerImpl member declared before every borrower and immutable after boot), value-type ResponseTierFilter copies, std::function members capturing server state, a function-local RefusalLogThrottle and test-only RAII fixtures; every one is proven in the cpp-safety reports (cpp-safety.md and cpp-safety-p2.md under the run scratch directory). Informational attestation, not a defect; the policy floor for a Resource Ledger omission is satisfied by this row. Range note: the pre-rebase heads 08af0976b, 6e500efd5 and a5595d173 are tree-identical to their post-rebase equivalents 250319c56, fd41b7e59 and 7613b711a (message-only rebase).

trigger: a Forensics-tier plugin response arrives while any authenticated dashboard session is subscribed to the legacy live output stream
classification_rationale: the shared live output stream had no read tier at all, a missing control
summary: The legacy dashboard live output stream is shared by every session and carried rendered rows of Forensics-tier plugins to any subscriber. Pre-existing sibling of the original defect, surfaced because the diff made every stored-response reader take a tier. The fix publishes no row of a Forensics-tier plugin and, when the plugin set is unwired, no output row at all. Also raised as: arch-1 (architect; shown sec-1, not independent). Fixed by: fix(events): do not publish Forensics-tier plugin rows to the live output stream (2e7f73f99). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a policy whose check instruction names a Forensics-tier plugin
classification_rationale: a code comment stated such plugins are never operator-facing while the control branch contradicted it
summary: The policy evaluator read a check stored output through an unrestricted internal read and kept a bounded copy that the compliance routes and MCP serve below the Forensics tier; a new comment said such plugins are never operator-facing, which was false. Derived CRITICAL (I1 with E2), native HIGH; the derivation was not moved. The fix reads with the Forensics plugins excluded so a Forensics check scores unknown and stores no output, and corrects the comment. A separate follow-up (#6065) tracks the dispatch-side authorization of policy checks; it is not part of this finding fix. Copies stored before the upgrade are tracked as g8p2-comp-1a and g8p2-comp-1a-residual. Also raised as: cpx-1 (cpp-expert), arch-3 policy-evaluator part (architect), comp-3 (compliance-officer, HIGH if unfixed: the copy sat outside retention and erasure); all echoes were shown sec-2 and are not independent. Fixed by: fix(compliance): score a Forensics-plugin policy check unknown instead of reading its output (ec068391a). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a Forensics-tier plugin command ends with failure text that the tracker stores and publishes
classification_rationale: the execution tracker failure-text path had no tier, a missing control
summary: Per-agent failure text stored by the execution tracker reached the durable column, the event outbox, the execution bus, the executions drawer and MCP execution status for any Execution:Read holder, a lower tier than the plugin rows. Content volume from these plugins is unknown, hence native MEDIUM and derived HIGH. The fix keeps only a bounded machine token (or a fixed placeholder) at write and again at read for rows still inside the 24 hour command correlation. Residuals are tracked as g8-sec-1 (sibling sinks, fixed), UP-15 and g8-up-4. Also raised as: sec-6 (security-guardian, native LOW, first noted), sre-6 (sre, derived HIGH: write-side blanking leaves durable rows and the 24 hour outbox replay). Fixed by: fix(executions): keep only a bounded token as a Forensics plugin's tracker error text (101dfc09b). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a bundle with a Forensics-tier step polled by a caller who holds a dispatch approval but not Forensics:Read; a result set built from a Forensics execution
classification_rationale: two operator-visible readers were classified internal and had no tier
summary: Bundle collation and the result-set materialiser were classified as internal consumers with no read tier although their results reach operators (bundle output through REST and MCP, set membership computed from output content). Derived HIGH (I1), native MEDIUM. Owner ruling: a dispatch approval does not imply read, and a result set sourced from a Forensics execution materialises empty for every creator. Bundle collation later also audits as response.forensics.read (surface=bundle). Also raised as: arch-3 bundle and materialiser parts (architect, derived HIGH), cons-9 (consistency-auditor parity note). Fixed by: fix(bundles): apply the caller's Forensics tier when collating bundle output (047064217); fix(result-sets): never derive materialised membership from Forensics-plugin rows (4626c2bb9); feat(responses): bundle collation audits a served Forensics step as response.forensics.read (bfa085746). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: the authorization or management-group read fails while the Forensics tier is resolved for an otherwise authorized caller
classification_rationale: the degrade produced a plausible result with no signal, a missing signal
summary: The first resolver turned any scoped-read failure into a present-empty set, so an authorized caller received a 200 with Forensics rows silently missing and no marker or metric naming the surface. The fix is a tri-state resolver: an unresolved decision answers a retryable 503 (REST, legacy), a retryable internal error (MCP) or a visible notice (dashboard surfaces), counts yuzu_server_forensics_tier_withheld_total{reason}, logs a throttled WARN and raises the YuzuForensicsTierUnresolved alert. One owner-disclosed exception remains (UP2-3). Also raised as: sre-1 (sre, derived HIGH; shown UP-1). Fixed by: fix(responses): answer 503 when the Forensics visibility cannot be resolved (62c560f5e); feat(observability): count and alert on withheld Forensics-tier reads (941e51e48). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: the executions drawer is opened while the authorization read degrades, or by a token session
classification_rationale: the notice and the comment named the wrong cause and the wrong probe
summary: The drawer used the loud global-only Response:Read probe and, on a degrade, told the operator the permission was required, concealing the real state; it also wrote a denial row per refresh for cookie sessions and ignored management-group confinement for scoped holders. The fix uses the quiet fleet-read probe, a distinct notice for an unconfirmed decision and no store read on a denial. Also raised as: sec-4 (security-guardian, native MEDIUM), arch-5 (architect). Fixed by: fix(executions): quiet Response:Read probe on the drawer, with its own notice on a degrade (10b88f2bf). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: hardware Actions poll of a Forensics-tier action by a user whose legacy role is administrator but whose RBAC roles lack Forensics:Read, enforcement on
classification_rationale: the UI reported a timeout while the device had replied
summary: The poll ended with a false "Timed out waiting for a response" although the device replied, because the tier filter returned zero rows for that caller. Derived HIGH (I3), native MEDIUM. The fix shows a permission notice on every attempt for a Forensics plugin the caller cannot read and an unconfirmed-permission notice on an unresolved decision. Fixed by: fix(hardware): permission notice on the result poll instead of a false timeout (f5afa58ae); test(hardware): a grant withdrawn between two polls ends the poll with the permission notice (8856797e9). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a reader relies on the claim that the tier covers every response read path
classification_rationale: documents and READMEs claimed coverage the code did not provide
summary: Claims that the tier covers every response read path (changelog fragment, upgrading guide, RBAC guide, REST guide, five plugin READMEs) were false while the live output stream and tracker failure text were unfiltered (I6 false assurance). Closed together with sec-1 and arch-2 and by rewording to enumerated paths with listed residuals. Also raised as: ent-2 (enterprise-readiness, HIGH conditional). Fixed by: fix(events): do not publish Forensics-tier plugin rows to the live output stream (2e7f73f99); fix(executions): keep only a bounded token as a Forensics plugin's tracker error text (101dfc09b); docs: authz model, ladder, observability and SOC 2 inventory for the Forensics tier (9fa7d9424); docs(user-manual): Forensics tier, ForensicsAnalyst role and their consequences (fea0068d4); docs(plugins): the five Forensics plugin READMEs state the tier's real coverage (e3871ccf7). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a reader or agentic worker follows the documented management-group scoped Forensics:Read path with an MCP-tier token
classification_rationale: user manuals and MCP descriptions stated a scoped grant that MCP-tier callers cannot use
summary: The manuals and the three MCP tool descriptions said a management-group scoped Forensics:Read is honoured; the resolver deliberately skips the scoped branch for service-scoped tokens, engine principals and MCP-tier tokens, so typical MCP callers need a global grant. Kept at HIGH (security-relevant behaviour concealed; docs-writer raised it for adjudication, no non-author adjudicator was available). Fix: one stated rule in the manuals, the MCP descriptions and OpenAPI text. Fixed by: docs(api): MCP tool descriptions and OpenAPI text state the Forensics tier accurately (0d1f5682b); docs(user-manual): Forensics tier, ForensicsAnalyst role and their consequences (fea0068d4). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: an agentic worker reads an empty query_responses result for a caller without Forensics:Read
classification_rationale: the tool description said zero rows means no match, which is false for withheld rows
summary: The MCP description said zero rows without retry_after_ms means no rows currently match, which is false for tier-withheld rows (A5 question c); the scoped-grant sentence was unreachable for MCP bearer sessions. Fix: the four response tools now say an empty or short result does not prove no data exists and state the global-grant rule. Also raised as: ent-5 (enterprise-readiness, MEDIUM, A5 empty-result meaning). Fixed by: docs(api): MCP tool descriptions and OpenAPI text state the Forensics tier accurately (0d1f5682b). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: an operator follows the "Grant Forensics:Read" remedy; only Administrator holds the grant, RBAC off means no grant is possible, and custom role authoring is unavailable
classification_rationale: the upgrade guide gave no in-product path for the remedy it prescribed
summary: The upgrade remedy had no in-product path (Forensics:Read was seeded only to Administrator, custom role authoring is not implemented, RBAC off allows no grant). Raised to HIGH as a concealed migration step. The fix seeds a delegable read-only system role ForensicsAnalyst, assignable fleet-wide through the audited A2 surface, and rewrites the guide for the three cases (RBAC off, RBAC on, scoped). Fixed by: feat(rbac): seed a delegable ForensicsAnalyst system role (2bbe67142); docs(rbac): add ForensicsAnalyst to the System Roles table (193e54a51); docs(user-manual): Forensics tier, ForensicsAnalyst role and their consequences (fea0068d4); docs(rbac): ForensicsAnalyst breadth and the unsupported hand-written scoped grant (8e215ef6c). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a later edit drops a setter or copies a resolver lambda that returns unrestricted
classification_rationale: no test observed the server.cpp wiring of the resolver and plugin set into the surfaces
summary: Nothing tested the server.cpp wiring of the resolver into the surface classes; route tests set the caller by hand, so a dropped setter stayed green. Recorded SHOULD by the missing-test-with-bounded-blast-radius rule. Fix: a lexical wiring gate over server.cpp with a mutation selftest. Impact recorded I9 with label SHOULD: a missing test with a bounded blast radius is SHOULD, not a floor. Fixed by: test(forensics): lexical gate pins the Forensics tier wiring in server.cpp (97941af91). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a later edit adds exclude(set, nullopt) or for_fixed_plugin_poll(nullptr) outside the frozen sites
classification_rationale: two unrestricted spellings and a substring match were not frozen by the tripwire
summary: The tripwire froze only unrestricted_internal_consumer(); exclude(set, nullopt) and for_fixed_plugin_poll(nullptr) were unfrozen unrestricted spellings and the type check was a weak substring. Fix: the tripwire rejects literal-unrestricted filters and freezes four internal-consumer sites. Impact recorded I9 with label SHOULD: a missing test with a bounded blast radius is SHOULD, not a floor. Fixed by: test(responses): tripwire freezes four internal-consumer sites and rejects literal-unrestricted filters (0f20b6584); test(responses): tripwire also rejects value-initialised VisibleSet and std::optional spellings (bf462a784). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a later edit deletes the engine or MCP-tier skip condition in the resolver
classification_rationale: resolver skip rules had no test, so deleting a skip condition stayed green
summary: Deleting the is_engine or mcp_tier skip conditions in the resolver kept the tests green. Fix: tests for scoped grant with service-scoped, MCP-tier and engine callers, degraded RBAC store and unwired inputs. Impact recorded I9 with label SHOULD: a missing test with a bounded blast radius is SHOULD, not a floor. Fixed by: test(forensics): pin the resolver's skip rules for service-scoped, MCP-tier and engine callers (bf87a1800). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a fix for sec-1, sec-2, sec-3 or arch-2 lands without a regression test
classification_rationale: regression tests for sec-1 to sec-3 and arch-2 had to ship with their fixes
summary: No tests existed for the live output stream, policy evaluator, bundle collation, tracker error text or drawer denial rows. Fix: each leak closure shipped with exact-output tests including ordinary-plugin controls. Impact recorded I9 with label SHOULD: a missing test with a bounded blast radius is SHOULD, not a floor. Fixed by: fix(events): do not publish Forensics-tier plugin rows to the live output stream (2e7f73f99); fix(executions): keep only a bounded token as a Forensics plugin's tracker error text (101dfc09b); fix(compliance): score a Forensics-plugin policy check unknown instead of reading its output (ec068391a); fix(bundles): apply the caller's Forensics tier when collating bundle output (047064217). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a plugin name containing non-ASCII characters under a locale-aware database
classification_rationale: the SQL fold and the C++ fold disagreed for non-ASCII input
summary: The SQL lower(plugin) used the database locale while the C++ set folded ASCII only, three separate folds existed, and a dash in a plugin name would split differently across parsers. Fix: lower(plugin COLLATE "C"), one shared ASCII fold, a catalogue soundness check that refuses boot on a dashed Forensics plugin or a plugin on two securables. Also raised as: arch-7 (architect), cpx-5 (cpp-expert). Fixed by: fix(responses): close the unwired-poll hatch, fold plugin names as ASCII in SQL, refuse an unsound catalogue (c7245f918); test(responses): pin the catalogue soundness check for a per-plugin response tier (e7212c77f). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a future caller passes a null plugin set to for_fixed_plugin_poll
classification_rationale: the unwired fixed-plugin poll factory defaulted to no clause, a missing fail-closed default
summary: for_fixed_plugin_poll(nullptr) meant no filter clause (an unwired set read as unfiltered) and one site hand-rolled refuse_unwired. Production wiring is unconditional so nothing was reachable. Fix: the factory returns refuse_unwired on null, the literal spelling is forbidden by the tripwire and the lexical gate. Also raised as: cps-1 (cpp-safety), cpx-4 (cpp-expert), sec-5 second half (security-guardian). Fixed by: fix(responses): close the unwired-poll hatch, fold plugin names as ASCII in SQL, refuse an unsound catalogue (c7245f918); test(responses): tripwire freezes four internal-consumer sites and rejects literal-unrestricted filters (0f20b6584). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a reviewer reads the SOC 2 inventory or the remote_access_audit routed row
classification_rationale: stale statements contradicted the post-fix behaviour
summary: Statements that stored Forensics results are readable by any Response:Read holder, that the gap is tracked and not re-gated, and the routed row clause citing #4990 as a known gap survived the change. Fix: inventory rows, ladder and routed row rewritten. The erasure-source and plugin-inventory part of comp-1 was closed later (g8p2-comp-2). Also raised as: arch-6 and plug-1 (stale docs), ent-4 (enterprise-readiness), comp-1 (compliance-officer). Fixed by: docs: authz model, ladder, observability and SOC 2 inventory for the Forensics tier (9fa7d9424); docs(routed-concerns): add the Forensics-tier row and correct the A2 assignable-role count (ea521ab60); docs(plugins): the five Forensics plugin READMEs state the tier's real coverage (e3871ccf7). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: an API token or MCP token holding Response:Read but not Forensics:Read reads stored responses
classification_rationale: the audit and upgrade documents were silent about token-caller denial rows
summary: Token readers without Forensics:Read write an auth.permission_required denial row per read (the quiet probe withholds the row only for cookie sessions); the audit-log and upgrade guides said nothing. Owner ruling: the noise is accepted. Fix: stated in the audit-log, upgrade, RBAC, REST and MCP guides. Also raised as: sre-3 (sre, volume), comp-5 (compliance-officer), g8-doc-1 (carry of doc-3). Fixed by: docs(user-manual): denial rows, residuals and cross references for the Forensics tier (e5f190f82); docs(audit-log): count semantics, denial-row volume, filter-bar exclusion, role count (382aaf9ea); docs(user-manual): Forensics tier, ForensicsAnalyst role and their consequences (fea0068d4). Closure re-verified by the Gate 8 pass 2 reviewer.

trigger: a management-group confined Response:Read holder opens the executions drawer
classification_rationale: the guides said confined callers see in-scope data on the drawer while the probe was global only
summary: The drawer probe was a global-only require_permission, so a scoped Response:Read holder lost the responses section while the RBAC guide said confined callers see in-scope data. Fixed by the quiet fleet-read probe and by the corrected guides. Fixed by: fix(executions): quiet Response:Read probe on the drawer, with its own notice on a degrade (10b88f2bf); docs(user-manual): Forensics tier, ForensicsAnalyst role and their consequences (fea0068d4). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a reviewer relies on the ladder claim about internal consumers
classification_rationale: the ladder said internal consumers are none of them an operator surface
summary: The ladder said no internal consumer is an operator surface although bundle collation and the result-set materialiser were. Rewritten to the four frozen internal-consumer sites that return no raw rows to an operator. Fixed by: docs: authz model, ladder, observability and SOC 2 inventory for the Forensics tier (9fa7d9424); docs(ladder): the four internal-consumer reads return no raw rows to an operator (7613b711a). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: an operator on the shipped default (RBAC enforcement off) follows "Grant Forensics:Read"
classification_rationale: no note that RBAC off permits no grant
summary: The remedy omitted that with enforcement off no grant is possible. Fix: an RBAC-off bullet in the upgrade, RBAC, REST and MCP guides (later extended with the enforcement consequences, see g8-ent2-1). Fixed by: docs(user-manual): Forensics tier, ForensicsAnalyst role and their consequences (fea0068d4). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: an operator upgrades without reading the behaviour change
classification_rationale: the changelog fragment did not lead with a Breaking note and the upgrade section lacked rollback, symptom and checklist content
summary: The changelog fragment lacked a Breaking lead and the drawer clause, and the upgrade section lacked rollback, symptom, hardware-poll, approval-path and checklist content. Fix: fragment rewritten with a Breaking lead; upgrade guide sections added. Also raised as: ent-3 (enterprise-readiness, MEDIUM). Fixed by: docs(changelog): Forensics tier fragment leads with Breaking and covers the full scope; add the role fragment (9043309e6); docs(user-manual): Forensics tier, ForensicsAnalyst role and their consequences (fea0068d4). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a later change to a ResponseStore read without the invariant loaded
classification_rationale: a required routed-concern row for the new read-chokepoint invariant was missing
summary: The new invariant (every ResponseStore read takes a tier filter, four frozen internal sites, proof via has_permission never require_fleet_read) had no routed-concern row; the two larger tables had no room. Fix: a row in the software-estate table, and the A2 row role count corrected. Also raised as: arch-8 (architect). Fixed by: docs(routed-concerns): add the Forensics-tier row and correct the A2 assignable-role count (ea521ab60). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a reader meets the nits
classification_rationale: wording and placement nits in several documents
summary: Wording nits: mcp.md Forensics text in the permission column, audit-log ordering and conjunction, an em dash in dashboard_routes.hpp, missing notes in mcp-server.md and response-store.md. Carried into Gate 8 as g8-doc-3, g8-doc-6, g8-doc-7 and g8-doc-9 and closed there; one em dash remains in the routed table header convention (g8p2-doc-2). Also raised as: plug-2 (plugin-developer, README sentence on aggregate and facet reads, closed by the README rewording). Fixed by: docs(mcp-server): state the Forensics tier on the response tools in one place (fd5fe215d); docs(user-manual): denial rows, residuals and cross references for the Forensics tier (e5f190f82); docs(code): neutral wording on the policy-check comments; role-count comments; em dash (1c62245ac). Closure re-verified by the Gate 8 pass 2 reviewer.

trigger: a reviewer counts or attributes response.forensics.read rows by surface
classification_rationale: the audit detail named no serving surface
summary: The audit detail lacked a serving-surface token. Fix: a closed server-chosen surface token (rest, legacy, mcp, dashboard, drawer, executions_page, hardware, bundle) on every row. Fixed by: feat(audit): name the serving surface on response.forensics.read (10499632a). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a reviewer compares the set-and-proceed MCP read with the fail-closed app-usage read

summary: The split between fail-closed REST, set-and-proceed MCP and dashboard persistence was not recorded as a decision. summary: Placeholder 0000- changelog names, an undated replacement sentence in authz-model.md, commit-message residue and the missing governance ledger fragment. The ledger fragment now exists (this file). The remaining items (placeholder rename after the PR number exists, commit-body residue) are carried as g8-doc-10 and g8-ent2-2.

trigger: the executions page renders in the degraded state after Forensics rows were counted
classification_rationale: the drawer audit claimed served rows for a degraded render
summary: The page-branch drawer audited Forensics rows it had counted even when the render degraded and served none, over-reporting. Fix: no note when the state is degraded, in both render branches. Fixed by: fix(executions): a degraded page read audits no Forensics rows it did not serve (40b80f2e2). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a caller without Forensics:Read opens the dashboard filter bar on a large response table
classification_rationale: a measured cost, no defect in output
summary: Facet reads for callers without Forensics:Read go through an EXISTS on the responses table: 5 to 10 times slower per call (worst observed about 2 s per column in a non-parallel plan crossover on a 5M row table), planner dependent, correct. No index recommended; the alternative rewrite measured worse. Accepted limit; revisit trigger is a filter bar render above 1 s at production table sizes. Also raised as: g8-perf-2 (performance, pass 1).

trigger: aggregate or distinct-agent reads lose the index-only scan under the tier clause
classification_rationale: a measured cost, no defect in output
summary: Aggregate and distinct-agent reads lose the index-only scan under the tier clause (about 10 ms to 100 ms at 100k rows per instruction), and an all-Forensics instruction costs about 80 to 105 ms per page read. The single-target contract makes the 100k row all-Forensics shape unlikely. Accepted. Also raised as: perf-4 (performance), g8-perf-3 (pass 1).

trigger: RBAC enforced and a caller without a global Forensics:Read, or with a scoped grant
classification_rationale: a cost, not a wrong output
summary: The resolver issues three uncached queries per request for an RBAC-enforced non-holder, plus a subtree query and an exempt-agent array bind for a scoped holder. The hardware poll arm was closed by resolving only for a Forensics plugin; the remainder (a negative cache keyed on user and RBAC write generation) is optional. Also raised as: sre-4 (sre), g8-perf-4 (pass 1), g8-sre-5 (pass 2). Related change (does not close the finding): perf(hardware): resolve Forensics visibility only for a Forensics plugin's result poll (0601f504d). Parked as a candidate follow-up; no issue has been filed by this ledger, the issue number is pending. Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: on-call reads the YuzuAuditPersistFailures description

summary: The alert text omitted response.forensics.read. Fix: the description names the verb and the fail-closed versus set-and-proceed split (the bundle surface was added later, g8-doc-2). Fixed by: feat(observability): count and alert on withheld Forensics-tier reads (941e51e48). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

summary: Six runbook sentences were missing: rollback re-exposure, RBAC-off remedy, troubleshooting entry, break-glass, the start-up refusal token, and denial-row volume. classification_rationale: noise, not a wrong output
summary: response.forensics.read is written on every live drawer refresh, as execution.detail.view already is; no new class of noise. Accepted at I8. Deduplication per (principal, execution, surface, minute) is an optional improvement. Also raised as: UP2-14 (unhappy-path, pass 2).

trigger: a reviewer relies on the ordering claim
classification_rationale: the audit-log said the verb row follows the neighbouring row, which is false for the drawer and visualization
summary: The audit-log ordering claim was false for the drawer and the visualization route and target_type spelling differed ("Execution" versus "execution"). Fix: ordering and target type documented. Also raised as: g8-cons-9 residual (INFO, documented). Fixed by: docs(user-manual): Forensics tier, ForensicsAnalyst role and their consequences (fea0068d4); docs: bundle collation is audited as response.forensics.read (surface=bundle); drop the known-gap statements (fd41b7e59). Closure re-verified against the code by the Gate 8 reviewers (passes 1 and 2).

trigger: a maintainer relies on the comments to learn which gate precedes the derivation
classification_rationale: false comments beside authz branches
summary: False comments: the MCP preview comment named the wrong gate, and a server.cpp comment claimed a byte-identical shape that changed. The server.cpp comment was reworded in the hatch commit; the two MCP comments were swapped in that edit and corrected later (g8-cons-2). Native MEDIUM; the impact is recorded by the recorder as I8 because the choice is the documented project convention. Documented in the audit header and the audit-log.

trigger: many API-token or MCP-tier callers without a global Forensics:Read poll response routes
classification_rationale: token callers write denial rows, owner accepted, saturation threshold never measured
summary: Each such read writes one auth.permission_required denial row; the REST routes are fail-closed on the audit write, so audit-path saturation could turn administrator reads into 503. The owner accepted the noise. The threshold was never measured: against a local database about 15k inserts per second, so far more than 2k token reads per second of headroom, but a remote database and the shared 16 connection pool change that. REVISIT TRIGGER (chaos-injector): if a real-server load run (200 token pollers at 5 req/s for 10 minutes) shows an administrator control reader receiving 503 with Sec-Audit-Failed, this re-derives to I5(b), HIGH and blocking. Not run. Also raised as: UP2-12, g8-up-3, g8-ch-4 (pass 2).

trigger: a non-conforming agent reports a command id that the server did not issue

summary: The tier decision rests on the plugin label stored with a row at ingest. Server-minted ids always carry the right label, so only a non-conforming agent is affected. The reviewer named this an I1 residual (requires a non-conforming agent, E4) and banded it LOW; the derivation from the recorded facts gives HIGH, so it is recorded BLOCKING and open pending owner adjudication (the reviewer LOW is kept as severity_native). Optional hardening: resolve the label from the dispatch record at ingest. Also raised as: UP2-11 (pass 2).

Fixed by: fix(hardware): permission notice on the result poll instead of a false timeout (f5afa58ae); test(hardware): a grant withdrawn between two polls ends the poll with the permission notice (8856797e9). trigger: a bundle containing a Forensics-tier step collated by a caller whose resolver answer is Denied (approval to dispatch does not imply read)
classification_rationale: owner-ruled behaviour with an unbounded client loop
summary: The filtered step collates as pending, so complete stays false and the manifest TTL slides on every poll, so an actively polled bundle is never evicted; an automated worker that follows retry_after_ms loops indefinitely, each poll costing the resolver reads, a collate query and for token callers a denial row. The owner ruled that filtered rows look absent. Mitigation candidates: a hard age cap for a manifest whose steps are terminal at the agent but withheld, a distinct withheld state (needs an owner ruling because of the existence signal), or a poll ceiling in the MCP twin. Documented (REST, MCP, upgrade guide). REVISIT TRIGGER: the shared connection pool saturating under bundle pollers re-derives this to I5(b), HIGH. Also raised as: UP2-1, g8-ch-5 (chaos-injector), g8-hp-2, g8-cons-6. Related change (does not close the finding): docs(rest-api): bundle polling for a caller who cannot read a Forensics step, Console notice (a9feee869); docs(mcp): disclosed exception, reading authority, bundle polling, audit posture difference, troubleshooting (d09bdce5e). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 2 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent; this row records the claim.

trigger: RBAC enforced; a caller without a global Forensics:Read reads ordinary data while the management-group store or its subtree query degrades
classification_rationale: an accepted fail-closed coupling with retry amplification
summary: The resolver always runs the three authorization reads (and a subtree expansion for any assignment) before the response query; an error yields Unknown(scope_read_failed) and every surface refuses a read that would not have needed Forensics. Under pool pressure each request adds up to three serial bounded acquires, and clients are told to retry. Native LOW (architect filed the same coupling as I8, g8-arch-4), derived MEDIUM (I5). Owner-accepted trade (UP-1: fail closed, never a partial 200); also the cost of KEEP in g8-arch-2 (e). Mitigation: resolve lazily, a negative cache per principal per generation, or treat ScopeReadFailed as Denied for callers with no scoped assignment. REVISIT TRIGGER: any production incident where a management-group store fault blocks ordinary response reads. Also raised as: UP2-4, g8-arch-4, g8-ch-3 (chaos-injector, live-fault shapes).

Closure if ever reopened: have the probe expose the degrade (tri-state from require_permission RBAC branch). Also raised as: g8-cons-4 (documentation scope, fixed). Related change (does not close the finding): docs(rest-api): policy check_result lifetime, disclosed exception, audit caveats, Console notice, count preview (db6c443c8); docs(mcp): disclosed exception, reading authority, bundle polling, audit posture difference, troubleshooting (d09bdce5e); docs(alerts): YuzuForensicsTierUnresolved comment names the one disclosed exception (29af3e603). summary: INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING keeps a pre-existing custom role of that name, merges the four read grants and leaves it assignable by name (including to an engine principal because the structural bar is is_system). One boot WARN per replica, no metric, no refusal; existing human assignees gain the four read grants at next boot with only the WARN. Owner ruling: WARN plus document. Documented in the RBAC and upgrade guides. Also raised as: g8-ch-9 (chaos-injector).

classification_rationale: speculative observability self-failure and alert shape
summary: Speculative: the counter increment takes the metrics registry lock on the request path in the degraded window; no counter exists for sanitiser substitutions, scrub lookup failures or denial rows. The alert-shape half (two refusals fired about 12 minutes in, a 5 minute outage fired 7 minutes after it ended) was fixed by rate(...[5m]) with for: 10m (see g8-sre-2). Also raised as: g8-ch-16. Related change (does not close the finding): fix(alerts): YuzuForensicsTierUnresolved tracks the failure window (5a4bfe846). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 2 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent; this row records the claim.

trigger: a late or replayed RUNNING frame arrives after a terminal row that was stored with raw text (written by an old replica or the pre-change binary)
classification_rationale: the persisted-row publish path was not covered by the reduction that the read paths apply
summary: The sticky-terminal upsert keeps the stored error text and its RETURNING value was published on the execution bus and appended to the 24 hour durable outbox without the scrub, even though every read accessor scrubs. Only rows stored raw are exposed (the rolling upgrade plus frames delayed across it). Nominal derivation I1 with E5, HIGH, native LOW; the reviewer requested owner adjudication because it is adjacent to but not named in the accepted rolling-upgrade residual. Fix: the returned value goes through the tracker error-text reduction (same plugin-set membership, fail closed on a failed lookup) inside the transaction before the outbox append and bus publish; a value already of token shape skips the lookup. Covered by an exact-output test with ordinary-plugin and token-shaped controls. Also raised as: UP2-20 (unhappy-path), g8-ch-1 (chaos-injector, HIGH if containment fails). Fixed by: fix(server): reduce the persisted error text before the tracker publishes it (939bea3ce). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 2 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent; this row records the claim.

trigger: a RUNNING frame for a (execution, agent) whose terminal row was stored raw

summary: Chaos scenario, HIGH if containment fails, blocking pending owner adjudication: the storage half was verified on a disposable database and the publish half was code-read. Same finding and same fix as g8-up-4, with a design for an exact-output test with controls. Observable signal today: none (no counter, audit row or log), so the test is the only control. Also raised as: g8-up-4. Fixed by: fix(server): reduce the persisted error text before the tracker publishes it (939bea3ce). trigger: sustained dispatch above about 5000 recorded commands per hour (the reap cap is 5000 rows per pass at about 60 minute cadence), or a failing correlation reap, while a list, drawer or status read carries a failed execution
classification_rationale: an unindexed scan on a table whose reaper has a drain ceiling, extending a shared-pool lease
summary: The read-side scrub scans command_execution (no execution_id index) once per tracker read that has non-empty error text: 38 to 88 ms at 1M rows, 263 to 628 ms at 10M, linear in the table. The reviewer corrected the premise "bounded by the 24 hour reaper": the reaper drains at most about 120,000 rows per day, so above about 1.4 recorded commands per second the table grows without bound and the new scan turns disk growth into read latency; a capped pass is invisible. Native LOW, derived MEDIUM (I5 unbounded growth base). Owner-accepted limit. REVISIT TRIGGER: command_execution live rows above about 1M, or p95 executions-list latency above 200 ms, or a capped correlation reap on three consecutive passes. No-migration mitigations: skip the lookup for a slot already of token shape, add a created_at range predicate on the existing index, cache the immutable "execution is Forensics" fact, and raise or make the reap cap adaptive with a capped-pass alert. Stale comment on the existing alert calls the table lower stakes. No issue filed by this ledger. Also raised as: g8-perf-1 (performance, LOW), g8-arch-7.

trigger: an agent status frame whose persisted error text is not bounded-token shaped reaches the tracker upsert while the Forensics execution lookup statement fails (statement timeout, cancel, a renamed or unreadable relation, backend loss)
classification_rationale: the fail-closed reading of a failed lookup held on the read paths but not inside the write transaction
summary: ROOT CAUSE SHARED BY SEVEN PASS 3 IDS (g8p3-cpx-1, g8p3-arch-1, g8p3-cps-1, g8p3-sec-1, g8p3-sre-1, g8-up3-1, g8p3-cons-2), introduced by the fix for g8-up-4 and g8-ch-1. The first form of that fix ran the Forensics execution lookup (a plain SELECT) on the upsert transaction's own connection, after the upsert and before the outbox append. A failed statement aborts a PostgreSQL transaction, so the lookup returned no answer, the text was reduced as intended, but the next statement (the outbox append) failed with an aborted-transaction error, the transaction rolled back and the agent's status was not recorded (the update is retried once and then logged as not recorded; agents do not re-send). Five reviewers reproduced the aborted-transaction behaviour on a disposable PostgreSQL 16; none ran the server binary against a faulted lookup. Because the guard compared against the sanitised form, the lookup also ran for every ordinary free-text failure frame (cost half: g8p3-sre-1b). Six reviewers (security-guardian, architect, cpp-expert, cpp-safety, sre, unhappy-path) derived it independently and none cites another; consistency-auditor and quality-engineer read the others first and are not counted. Fix in 92e0e60f5, read in the diff: the lookup runs only when the persisted text differs from the incoming text, under a SAVEPOINT rolled back on failure, so a failed lookup reduces the text while the status write, the outbox row and the bus event commit; the wiring gate pins the ingest-side reduction the skip relies on. The write-path fault case (g8p3-qe-2) was added in the same commit and 047b19be0 characterises the write path's trust in the ingest-reduced text. Primary row of the group. File and line are relative to 29af3e603 (1190). NOT verified: no governance agent has re-reviewed the fix; the SAVEPOINT release or rollback itself failing is logged only (not read as a hole by any reviewer); the sticky-terminal case still scans once inside the write transaction (g8p3-sre-1b). Fixed by: fix(tracker): a failed Forensics lookup can no longer lose an agent's status (92e0e60f5); test(tracker): characterise the write path's trust in the ingest-reduced text (047b19be0). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 3 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim.

trigger: a burst of ordinary-plugin failure frames with free-text error text while command_execution holds a large number of live rows (the lookup has no execution_id index)
classification_rationale: no bound on the cost of the lookup on the ingest hot path
summary: MITIGATED, NOT ELIMINATED. In the first form of the g8-up-4 fix the guard compared the persisted text with its sanitised form, which differs for any ordinary free-text failure, so every such frame ran one unindexed scan of command_execution inside the write transaction, holding the agent_exec_status row lock and a lease of the shared 16-connection pool. sre measured it on a disposable PostgreSQL 16 with a 1,000,000-row command_execution on a busy shared host (relative figures only): the lookup alone 32 to 37 ms, the upsert transaction 2.0 ms alone against 118.9 ms with the lookup under 16-way concurrency (about 59 times lower throughput); cpp-safety measured 8.6 ms at 100,000 rows. In 92e0e60f5 (read in the diff) the lookup is skipped whenever the persisted text equals the incoming, already reduced, text, which is every ordinary frame, so each reporter's stated trigger no longer produces the scan. Residuals: a persisted value that differs from the incoming one and is not already a bounded token (the sticky-terminal or older-writer case) still runs one scan inside the write transaction, now savepointed; and the read-side lookup is unchanged, an unindexed scan per tracker read that carries error text, tracked by g8-sre-1 (open, with its revisit trigger). No load run has been made after the change. Row left open so the residual is not read as closed. Mitigated by: fix(tracker): a failed Forensics lookup can no longer lose an agent's status (92e0e60f5). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 3 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim.

trigger: a future change adds a second caller of ExecutionTracker::update_agent_status, or rewrites the status text after the ingest reduction, so an unreduced Forensics failure text reaches the tracker write path
classification_rationale: a missing precondition statement and a missing pin on the single caller, not a contradiction in existing text
summary: ROOT CAUSE SHARED BY THREE PASS 4 IDS (g8p4-sec-1, g8p4-architect-1, g8p4-qe-4), raised independently by security-guardian, architect and quality-engineer (none cites another). The fix for the lost status write (92e0e60f5) made the tracker write path trust its caller to have reduced the failure text at ingest: it skips the Forensics lookup when the persisted text equals the incoming text. That precondition was stated nowhere on the declaration, a comment on set_forensics_plugin_set still described the earlier behavior, and the wiring gate pinned only one statement in notify_exec_tracker, nothing about the number of callers or about rewriting the status text after the reduction. Each reporter searched the tree and found exactly one production caller, so nothing is exposed at the reviewed head; the defect is that a second caller, or a rewrite after the reduction, would publish the unreduced text to the outbox and the bus on its first write (a characterization test documents this) while no gate fails. DERIVATION, stated because the reporters' codings differ: security-guardian coded I1 with E3, quality-engineer I3 with E5, architect I9 with a note that I6 applies only latently; each labeled it LOW. This row records the union of impacts (I1, I3, I6, I9) and exposures (E3, E5) and ADDS E6, which is the recorder's addition and no reporter's: the wrong outcome cannot occur in production at the reviewed head, because the only caller reduces the text and the gate pins that call. The E6 cap gives LOW, mapped NICE. Without E6 the I1 and I3 bases derive HIGH and the row would be BLOCKING; it is fixed either way, and adjudicated_by is not written. FIX: 26969cb80 states the precondition on the declaration and on AgentExecStatus::error_detail, corrects the set_forensics_plugin_set comment, and adds two wiring-gate pins (update_agent_status has exactly one call site, with same-named methods of other classes excluded by receiver; the status text in notify_exec_tracker is written exactly once) with selftest cases for a second caller in arrow, dot, split-line and pointer-to-member spellings. That commit staged two hunks of the gate at shifted positions so the gate file did not parse (see g8p4-bisect-26969cb80); a5fdc36ff restores it. Verified at 8a66c0cfd: the four Python gates print OK (wiring gate: 41 statements, 7 exact counts, 1 tracker-caller pin, 2 forbidden dumps; both selftests OK), and the fix author's mutation runs of the new pins (not committed) were red. NOT verified: no governance agent has re-reviewed the pins; the gate is lexical and cannot see a caller reached through a renamed wrapper. Primary row of the group. File and line are relative to 7e081bd7e. Fixed by: fix(tracker): state the ingest-reduced precondition and pin the single update_agent_status caller (26969cb80); fix(tests): place the update_agent_status caller pin and its selftest at the right lines (a5fdc36ff). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 4 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim, verified by this recorder in the commit diff.

trigger: a late RUNNING frame arrives after a terminal failure whose persisted text is free text (the sticky-terminal case), so the persisted text differs from the incoming empty text and is not a bounded token
classification_rationale: the equal-text shortcut removes the lookup from ordinary frames, not from this branch
summary: The equal-text shortcut removes the command_execution lookup from every ordinary first-write frame, but the sticky-terminal branch still runs one scan inside the write transaction (under the SAVEPOINT, with the agent_exec_status row lock held), even for an execution with no Forensics command. Frequency is bounded by how often late RUNNING frames follow a terminal frame, cost by 24 hours of command_execution rows. No correctness effect: the SAVEPOINT removes the lost-write mode. Read, not measured by this reviewer. This is the residual already recorded as g8p3-sre-1b, g8p3-cps-2 and g8-up3-2 (open) for the write side, and the read-side scan is g8-sre-1 (open); recorded here as a pass 4 re-derivation so the cost is not rediscovered as new. unhappy-path (its register row R4) and sre reached the same residual and call it rare. No change was made for it.

trigger: the SAVEPOINT statement, or the closing RELEASE or ROLLBACK TO, fails inside the agent-status write transaction (a connection-level fault between two statements)
classification_rationale: two defence-in-depth branches have no test
summary: Two branches of scrub_error_texts_in_txn are untested: the SAVEPOINT cannot be created (the text is reduced without a lookup) and the closing RELEASE or ROLLBACK TO fails (a warning only). Raised independently by cpp-expert (g8p4-cpx-1), cpp-safety (g8p4-cps-1, test half), unhappy-path (g8p4-up-1, test half), quality-engineer (g8p4-qe-5, untested-branch bullet) and sre (g8p4-sre-3). The fault fixture used by the write-path case renames a table, which fails only the lookup SELECT; reaching these statements needs connection-level fault injection, which the fix author left out rather than extend the fixture (stated in the 4a76b2d47 body). Both branches only reduce the text and log, and a connection that broken also fails the outbox append that follows, which the generic single retry handles, so no new loss mode exists. OPEN RESIDUAL, not a defect: no test guards a future edit to the two branches. The unthrottled warning half of the same reports is g8p4-cps-1 (fixed). Nothing in this row was changed by the fix wave.

trigger: a connection fault makes the closing RELEASE or ROLLBACK TO of the Forensics lookup savepoint fail on every frame of a burst
classification_rationale: one warning had no throttle and printed the driver's error text
summary: The warning for a failed RELEASE or ROLLBACK TO of the lookup savepoint was emitted once per frame, unlike its two sibling warnings, and printed the driver's error text. Raised by cpp-safety (g8p4-cps-1), unhappy-path (g8p4-up-1) and sre (g8p4-sre-1, the unthrottled-warning remark). The reporter's I2 note concerns the generic lost-write-on-connection-fault behavior that exists for any statement of the transaction and adds no exposure class, so it is not recorded as this finding's impact. Fixed in 4a76b2d47, read in the diff: the warning is throttled to one line a minute under its own key and no longer prints the driver text. The untested half of the same reports is g8p4-cpx-1 (open). Fixed by: fix(tracker): throttle the savepoint-close warning and assert exact rows on the write path (4a76b2d47). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 4 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim, verified by this recorder in the commit diff.

trigger: a source file uses a using-declaration for std::nullopt and passes a spaced scope token to the read filter
classification_rationale: an incomplete closure in a lexical gate: the pass 3 fix handled each feature alone, not both together
summary: The read tripwire re-qualified std names on the raw argument text before closing whitespace around the scope operator, so with a using-declaration in the file a spaced or line-split spelling of the no-restriction argument was not recognized. The reporter reproduced it with in-memory probes, and the selftest never combined the two features. Fixed in d9c387168, read in the diff: whitespace around every scope operator is closed first, and the selftest gains a case that combines them and fails against the previous script. Verified at 8a66c0cfd: the tripwire and its selftest print OK. The gate remains lexical. Fixed by: fix(tests): the read tripwire closes spaced scope tokens before re-qualifying std names (d9c387168). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 4 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim, verified by this recorder in the commit diff.

The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 4 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim, verified by this recorder in the commit diff.

trigger: an alternative of a new wiring-gate rule is weakened or dropped
classification_rationale: the wiring selftest stayed green when three of the new rules were weakened
summary: Mutating a copy of the gate (dropping the JSON-print alternative, the text-format alternative, the partial-serialization alternative, or loosening the accessor row to the dot spelling only) left the selftest green: it did not prove those rules fail on a crafted violation. The fix author's mutation runs (not committed) turned the selftest red for each dropped alternative and for the loosened accessor row. trigger: the write-path fault case is read as pinning the fix
classification_rationale: one section could not discriminate and the outbox and bus assertions were substring-level
summary: Three remarks about the write-path fault case. (1) The section for an already-reduced frame stays green under every mutant because the reduction is idempotent; relabeled as a control in 4a76b2d47. (2) The outbox and bus assertions were substring checks that would not catch a duplicated transition event; 4a76b2d47 asserts exact rows (one outbox row and one bus frame per step, the frame equal to the row, the stored value equal to the bounded value or to the text as written), and 368d9b431 then restricted the row counts to agent-transition events, because one status write also appends progress and completion events and the first form failed against a real database. (3) The two untested savepoint branches are g8p4-cpx-1 (open), and the process-static throttle key assumption is in g8p4-rollup (open). Fixed by: fix(tracker): throttle the savepoint-close warning and assert exact rows on the write path (4a76b2d47); fix(tests): the write-path rows are counted among agent-transition events only (368d9b431). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 4 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim, verified by this recorder in the commit diff.

trigger: a non-conforming agent reports a command id that the server did not issue
classification_rationale: the stored plugin is a function of the agent-echoed command id, an open design limit
summary: ADJUDICATION 2026-10-24 by Astra: FIX_REQUIRED (Astra proposed BAND_WRONG: CRITICAL; confidence medium). The tier decision rests on the plugin label stored with a row at ingest. Server-minted ids always carry the right label, so only a non-conforming agent is affected. The reviewer named this an I1 residual (requires a non-conforming agent, E4) and banded it LOW; the derivation from the recorded facts gives HIGH, so it is recorded BLOCKING and open pending owner adjudication (the reviewer LOW is kept as severity_native). Optional hardening: resolve the label from the dispatch record at ingest. Also raised as: UP2-11 (pass 2).
adjudicated_by: Astra (gpt-6-astra via the codex skill, read-only opine run on 2026-10-24; external to the authoring session; independence asserted, not enforced)
adjudication_rationale: The response classification is derived from metadata supplied by the agent daemon without an authoritative dispatch admission check on the inspected ingest paths. That classification controls stored response visibility and derived output handling. The finding remains valid and blocking. Closure requires authoritative attribution with conservative handling of unresolved provenance and regression evidence for both ingest paths. Smallest fix named: establish command provenance once before either ingest path stores or publishes ordinary responses, using server-authored command, plugin and target information; the existing best-effort expiring execution mapping is not sufficient by itself. A demonstrated upstream command and target admission check covering both paths would change the verdict. Lead note: Astra proposed raising this to CRITICAL by applying E2 because the reader gains information outside its starting authority. SKILL.md judges E2 by the privilege required to begin, never the privilege gained, and the same E2 question for the original defect (e2-original-defect-band) is reserved to the owner. So the exposure and severity_mapped stay as derived by the earlier rows (BLOCKING, open) and the CRITICAL proposal is recorded here for the owner to rule on together with e2-original-defect-band. The verdict (fix required, not closable as a documented residual) does not depend on the band.

SCOPE RE-CUT (Test 2), recorded 2026-10-24; the earlier rows of this finding, including the Astra run 1 FIX_REQUIRED row, are untouched. The envelope this finding was raised against carried an upgrade-protection claim (stored data written by earlier builds is protected when read). The project owner stated in the working session on 2026-10-24: "we're doing a hard cutover - an upgrade path is not needed". That statement is recorded as a SCOPE DECISION and is NOT an acceptance of any residual risk. No retrievable artefact exists for a spoken statement, so nothing in the repository verifies it beyond this recorder's transcription of it. The release now states a deployment contract in docs/user-manual/upgrading.md ('Deployment contract (hard cutover)', line 102 at 5add044d9) and the same contract in docs/authz-model.md section 4, docs/executions-history-ladder.md, the SOC 2 inventory and clause 8 of the Forensics routed-concern row: initial deployment into a fresh database only, no data imported from earlier builds, every server writer and serving replica on the new build, earlier binaries excluded, recovery by rolling forward or restoring this build's own backups into a fresh deployment. Those documents say in terms that the executable does NOT enforce the contract (it does not verify the provenance of the database it opens), so it is a procedural control, and that the release describes no upgrade path and makes no statement about what an earlier build stored. The withdrawn claim was stripped from the user documents, the SOC 2 inventory, the routed row and the changelog fragments (ff5856bd6, 341a1c8f9, 8db274679, d310f1642, 00e77b606). Astra run 2 ruled APPLIES_TO_CONTRACT on the conditions: a recorded deployment contract, consistent documentation, a ledger record that preserves the originals, and evidence that new writes stay protected. THE BAND IS NOT LOWERED: impact and severity_mapped are restated unchanged, and the earlier rows' band stands as the derived band for a deployment outside the contract. NARROWED TRIGGER: from 'a rolling upgrade, or an execution whose command correlation is older than 24 hours' to 'a deployment outside the contract in which failure text written by an earlier build, or an earlier-build writer, reaches the database'. WITHIN the contract: new ingest reduces recognised Forensics failure text to a bounded token before it is persisted (failure_text_for_sinks, applied before the tracker write on both ingest paths), independent of the 24 hour life of the dispatch record, so losing the record later cannot restore the original text; replicas on the new build republish already reduced payloads. Neither Astra run 2 nor the pass 5 reviewers found a raw-text path for a supported deployment. NOT claimed: the executable does not protect a database that violates the contract, and the read-time reduction in the tracker is defense in depth that works only while the dispatch record is held (a row with no record is returned as stored; forensics_error_detail.hpp). EVIDENCE, cases that exist at 5add044d9 (read by this recorder, not re-run in this session): test_forensics_ingest_leaks.cpp 'tracker error_detail: a Forensics plugin's free-text failure is stored as a bounded value', 'tracker error_detail: a later RUNNING frame never republishes a stored free-text value', 'terminal failure text: every derived sink carries only a bounded token for a Forensics-tier plugin', and 'tracker error_detail: rows written before the sanitizer are reduced on every read' (which pins the defense in depth and the as-stored behaviour of an unmapped row); test_response_provenance.cpp 'provenance ingest: a failure text for an id the server never issued is reduced in every sink' and 'provenance ingest: failure to record fails safe, and a reaped record is unverified'. UP-7, which also decides what new data is reduced, is closed by its own row. adjudicated_by: Astra (gpt-6-astra via the codex skill, read-only opine run 2 on 2026-10-24, after the cutover decision; external to the authoring session; independence asserted, not enforced). Separation that applied: Test 2, a scope change (the upgrade-protection claim withdrawn), adjudicated by a party that is not the change's author and did not raise this finding.
adjudication_rationale: New ingest reduces recognized Forensics failure text before tracker persistence, independently of the command correlation lifetime. Correlation expiry does not restore the original text, and republication between new replicas carries the already reduced payload. Historical raw rows and events remain readable if earlier databases, backups or writers enter the deployment. Rejection is justified only under an explicit fresh deployment contract excluding those sources, with consistent documentation and independent adjudication. This does not close UP-7 or assert that all new attribution is trustworthy.

summary: SCOPE RE-CUT (Test 2), recorded 2026-10-24; the earlier rows of this finding, including the Astra run 1 FIX_REQUIRED row, are untouched. The envelope this finding was raised against carried an upgrade-protection claim (stored data written by earlier builds is protected when read). The project owner stated in the working session on 2026-10-24: "we're doing a hard cutover - an upgrade path is not needed". That statement is recorded as a SCOPE DECISION and is NOT an acceptance of any residual risk. No retrievable artefact exists for a spoken statement, so nothing in the repository verifies it beyond this recorder's transcription of it. The release now states a deployment contract in docs/user-manual/upgrading.md ('Deployment contract (hard cutover)', line 102 at 5add044d9) and the same contract in docs/authz-model.md section 4, docs/executions-history-ladder.md, the SOC 2 inventory and clause 8 of the Forensics routed-concern row: initial deployment into a fresh database only, no data imported from earlier builds, every server writer and serving replica on the new build, earlier binaries excluded, recovery by rolling forward or restoring this build's own backups into a fresh deployment. Those documents say in terms that the executable does NOT enforce the contract (it does not verify the provenance of the database it opens), so it is a procedural control, and that the release describes no upgrade path and makes no statement about what an earlier build stored. The withdrawn claim was stripped from the user documents, the SOC 2 inventory, the routed row and the changelog fragments (ff5856bd6, 341a1c8f9, 8db274679, d310f1642, 00e77b606). Astra run 2 ruled APPLIES_TO_CONTRACT on the conditions: a recorded deployment contract, consistent documentation, a ledger record that preserves the originals, and evidence that new writes stay protected. THE BAND IS NOT LOWERED: impact and severity_mapped are restated unchanged, and the earlier rows' band stands as the derived band for a deployment outside the contract. NARROWED TRIGGER: from 'a policy check ran a Forensics-tier plugin before the upgrade; the policy is disabled, the agent is decommissioned or out of scope, so the pair is never rewritten' to 'a deployment outside the contract in which a policy status row written by an earlier build still holds check_result output of a Forensics-tier plugin'. WITHIN the contract: the evaluator's collector excludes Forensics responses before it derives a verdict or copies output (the SQL tier filter is applied before the query limit), and a missing filtered response leaves check_result empty, so a supported deployment never writes the copy; a Forensics check scores unknown. The earlier 'owner acceptance pending formal adjudication' wording in this finding is superseded: the owner's statement is a scope decision, not an acceptance, and no residual is accepted. Option (b) of the compliance reviewer (a one-time boot sweep) stays available if an upgrade path is ever supported. A separate follow-up (#6065) tracks the dispatch-side authorization of policy checks. EVIDENCE, cases that exist at 5add044d9 (read, not re-run here): test_policy_evaluator.cpp 'policy evaluator: a Forensics-plugin check scores unknown and stores no output (#4990)' and 'policy evaluator: an unwired Forensics plugin set scores every check unknown (#4990)'; the attribution those cases rely on is the server's dispatch record (UP-7, closed). Astra proposed CRITICAL by applying E2; the same reasoning as UP-15 applies and the E2 question stays with the owner. The earlier row said 'adjudicated_by is NOT written' beside an Astra name (run 1); that sentence belonged to the earlier row and does not apply to this one.

CLOSED. A response is no longer labelled by the command id an agent echoes. Every dispatch now writes a server-authored record (command id, plugin, execution id) at the single dispatch builder, after classification, authorization and the kill switch and before any send; both ingest paths resolve the label once per frame from that record (resolve_response_provenance) and hand it to the stored row, the live output stream, analytics, the tracker text, the registry audit and the failure-text reduction. A frame with no usable record (never issued, failed write, reaped after 24 hours, empty plugin, two failed reads) is stored under the unverified label, a member of the Forensics set, so it fails closed. Pass 5 reviewers who confirmed closure: security-guardian, architect, cpp-safety, cpp-expert, consistency-auditor, happy-path, unhappy-path (for the stated trigger), quality-engineer, compliance-officer. CAVEATS they gave, all recorded limits and not re-raised: (1) an id the server legitimately issued can be presented again by the endpoint it was sent to, so that endpoint can still influence the label among catalogue plugins by that route, but it can no longer invent a label and the stored label is always a catalogue plugin or the sentinel; (2) a failed record write, a record reaped after 24 hours or a degraded read stores that dispatch's responses under the unverified label, withheld from callers without Forensics:Read and counted (yuzu_server_response_provenance_total, yuzu_exec_correlation_write_degrade_total); (3) unrecorded registry ids mint no registry.write audit row; (4) the gateway path could bind a response to the request's own id and does not (architect, see g8p5-unnumbered-notes). Pass 5 raised follow-ups on the new record, each in its own row: g8p5-quality-engineer-1 (fixed), g8p5-architect-1, g8p5-unhappy-1, g8p5-unhappy-3 (open). trigger: an engine-kind session holding a global Forensics:Read grant reads on a replica whose cached enabled flag is stale-false while RBAC enforcement is on (another replica enabled it, or the local refresh is failing)
classification_rationale: the engine branch lacked the typed unavailable outcome that the ordinary RBAC branch has
summary: require_permission's engine branch decided 'RBAC is off' from the raw cached enabled flag, short-circuiting before the typed permission check. With a stale-false flag the typed check never ran, the gate answered a definitive 403, the Forensics resolver mapped that to Denied and every surface served a successful response with the Forensics rows silently missing (no 503, no marker): the UP2-3 outcome for the engine caller class, and the new documents promised it away. The ordinary RBAC branch already decided from the enforcement view, which treats a stale or degraded view as enforced. DERIVED HIGH (I3 base HIGH; E4 and E5 do not lower it; E6 not claimed, the window is not proven impossible); the reporters' native bands were MEDIUM and LOW. Also raised as: g8p5-cps-1 (cpp-safety, native LOW, derivation HIGH; neither report cites the other). FIX: the engine branch now decides the definitive refusal from rbac_enforcement_in_effect exactly like the ordinary branch, so a stale or degraded view runs the typed check and the opt-in mapping answers the retryable 503; the default mapping answers what it answered before; the raw-flag lexical allowlist keeps its two remaining engine sites and now pins their count. Tests (test_authz_topology_floor.cpp, case 'an engine principal's gate decides RBAC is off from the enforcement view'): a fresh disabled view is a definitive 403 under both mappings; enforced with a failing role query is 503 opted in and 403 by default; a healthy granted engine is admitted; a stale-false view whose refresh succeeds adopts the enable and admits the granted engine; a stale-false view whose refresh keeps failing is Unknown opted in and 403 by default. BEHAVIOUR NOTE FOR THE RE-REVIEW: a degraded or stale view whose typed check finds a grant now ADMITS the engine principal where the raw-flag line answered 403. That widening matches what the ordinary branch already does and is intended, but it is a change to an authorization decision and a targeted security-guardian recheck of it is OWED (gate8-pass5-pending). Fixed by: fix(auth): the engine-principal gate decides "RBAC is off" from the enforcement view (b3293b2d8). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 5 (reviewed head da7835d5c) and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass5-pending); this row records the claim, verified by this recorder in the commit diff and at 5add044d9.

trigger: a Guardian rule push, a per-agent reconcile push or an asset-tag push to many agents while the shared PostgreSQL pool is contended or exhausted
classification_rationale: no batched or deferred record for the per-agent fan-out loops; nothing is contradicted
summary: The dispatch record is one synchronous single-attempt upsert inside build_classified_command. Three callers mint one command id PER AGENT in a loop that wrote nothing to PostgreSQL before: the operator Guardian push (server.cpp:21611 loop), the heartbeat reconcile push (6187) and the asset-tag push (14069-14100); lines as read at da7835d5c. So a push to N agents does N serial upserts on the calling thread, and gateway-queued frames wait on them because forward_gateway_pending() runs only after the loop (server.cpp:21655). The bound comment said 'one kWriteTimeout', true per dispatch and false per push (the bound itself is g8p5-sre-2, fixed). `__guard__.push_rules` is a protective action: this DELAYS it and never refuses it (the record returns void and dispatch proceeds). Also, on the direct Subscribe path a solicited `__guard__` reply is dropped at agent_service_impl.cpp:1534 by the agent-set plugin field BEFORE provenance is read, so for a direct agent that record is written and never read. MEASURED FLOORS, not production figures: 0.08 to 0.16 ms per statement with fsync off on loopback (architect, performance, sre; about 41 s for 500,000 agents on one box); with default durability on a shared box a single client measured mean 15 ms and p99 360 ms (performance); one multi-row insert of 5,000 rows took 67 to 258 ms. The contended case was not measured. Also raised as: g8p5-performance-2 (performance, native LOW), g8p5-unhappy-4 defect 1 (unhappy-path, native LOW) and a note by happy-path. OPEN (SHOULD). Verified unfixed at 5add044d9: record_command_dispatch has one call site (server.cpp:13058) and no loop-level batching or skip exists. CANDIDATES, not prescriptions: skip the record for `__guard__` (an unrecorded replayed `__guard__` id would then fail closed as unverified; the gateway-path reply handling needs a check first), issue the per-agent records of one push as one multi-row statement before the loop, or move forward_gateway_pending() ahead of the writes. No latency figure is to be stated in the documents.

trigger: the dispatch-record lease is acquired and the INSERT then stalls (a lock held on the table, a commit stall, a half-open connection)
classification_rationale: the comments said 'at most one kWriteTimeout' while kWriteTimeout bounds only the pool lease acquire
summary: The stated bound on the dispatch-time write was false: kWriteTimeout (2000 ms) bounds try_acquire_for only; the statement then runs under the pool's server-side lock_timeout (10 s) and statement_timeout (30 s). Measured by sre: with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held on the table the exact upsert blocked 10.04 s then failed with a lock timeout. Wrong in three places (server.cpp, execution_tracker.hpp, the ladder). Also raised as: g8p5-cons-4 (consistency-auditor), g8p5-unhappy-4 defect 2 (unhappy-path; truth half). FIX: comment and documentation only, behaviour unchanged. The comments now state that the lease wait is about 2 s and a held table lock blocks the write for about 10 s before it fails (30 s for a wedged statement). The cost side of the same push loops is g8p5-architect-1 (open). Fixed by: docs(tracker): the dispatch-record write is bounded by the pool timeouts, not by kWriteTimeout (4e9249f5a); docs(retention): dispatch-record write bound, reap statement and alerts (828ffb2a1). classification_rationale: no inflow bound exists on the new per-dispatch record; the authors' sizing models rows per agent per fleet event, not a caller-driven rate

trigger: a command_execution row whose plugin is empty (written by a binary that predates migration 6, or by any writer that omits the column) is later refreshed by record_command_dispatch (a re-drive of the same stable id)

Candidates: set the plugin when the stored one is empty (still immutable once set) with one test, or state it under the contract paragraph in the upgrade guide.

trigger: a record read that fails twice in a row (pool exhaustion or a query error) for a frame whose record exists
classification_rationale: residuals of the accepted record-write limit, with a different trigger
summary: Residuals of the lookup_degraded path: (i) the retry is immediate with no backoff, so a starved pool is hit twice back to back and one frame stalls the Subscribe reader up to 3 s; (ii) the label is written into the stored row and nothing relabels it once the pool recovers, so the loss is permanent although the record exists; (iii) the DEX per-device and device-live pollers and the TAR scan result read through the fixed-plugin tier, so an unverified reply ends in the 'No response from the device (timed out)' text with no notice; (iv) yuzu_exec_correlation_read_degrade_total counts per attempt, so a per-frame rate reading on it is doubled, and every `__keepalive__` frame was counted in the outcome counter, one unrecorded per keepalive interval for the life of a command. FIXED: (iv) keepalive frames no longer move the outcome counter or raise the unverified-response line (29027fcf5) and the per-attempt counting is stated in the metrics row (088841b8d). OPEN, verified unfixed at 5add044d9: (i) backoff, (ii) a repair pass that relabels rows whose command id now resolves, (iii) a notice on the DEX and device-live pollers. Fixed by: fix(provenance): throttle the dispatch-record failure log; a keepalive labels nothing (29027fcf5); docs(metrics): dispatch-record counters, alerts and role-query accounting (088841b8d).

trigger: a degraded dispatch-record store while a push other than the operator Guardian push loop runs, or a latched loop that trips on one spurious failure

summary: Residuals of the g8p5-architect-1 fix, all OPEN and none claimed closed. (1) The heartbeat reconcile push (send_push, server.cpp around :6192) is not given the short budget: it is one write per call, not a loop, and the pool clamps an acquire on a saturated pool to 500 ms; the wiring gate pins that lambda's text in about 27 places, so changing it is a larger edit. The asset-tag push (push_asset_tags_to_agent) is likewise one write per call and keeps the 2 s budget. (2) There is no per-statement SET LOCAL: once a connection is leased the pool's lock_timeout (10 s) and statement_timeout (30 s) apply, paid once per latched loop and once per call everywhere else; adding it needs four round trips instead of one on the healthy path of every agent in the loop. (3) Skipped writes label the replies of a gateway-routed __guard__ command ~unverified (counted, fail closed, no disclosure); a single spurious failure early in a loop therefore costs the rest of that one loop its record labels. (4) 'Every agent still receives its command after a skipped write' is not asserted behaviourally: the record write returns void before the send, and the wiring gate pins the unconditional return. Figures for (1) and (2) are as stated in dispatch_record_policy.hpp and the wave N1 report; (3) and (4) are the documented behaviour read in the header and the commit message.

classification_rationale: queue residence time versus the 24 hour dispatch-record window is not traced
summary: Open INFO lead from the wave N2 investigation; epistemic status speculative because the path was not traced. The server sets no wire expiry on a command, and gateway-pending commands are drained by the forwarding loops (forward_gateway_pending); that drain was not traced for queues that last a day or more. If a command were delivered more than 24 hours after its record (the reaper deletes records older than that), its responses would be stored with the ~unverified label and withheld from readers without Forensics:Read: fail closed, no disclosure, but a visible gap. The delay and stagger inputs are bounded far inside the window (g8p7-fable-delay-bound); this lead concerns queueing, not those inputs. OPEN.

The exposure itself is the one recorded at I1/BLOCKING on g8p5-astra-2; this row records only the asymmetry and that no bound exists, banded NICE because inside the contract no such row exists. OPEN.
