trigger: sustained dispatch above about 5000 recorded commands per hour (the reap cap is 5000 rows per pass at about 60 minute cadence), or a failing correlation reap, while a list, drawer or status read carries a failed execution
classification_rationale: an unindexed scan on a table whose reaper has a drain ceiling, extending a shared-pool lease
summary: CLOSED OUT of this change and carried by Issue 2 (dispatch-record hardening). The work is real and is not done here; it is owed by the follow-up, not by this PR. The remaining work is item(s) of Issue 2 (dispatch-record hardening) in followup-issues-draft-v3.md (the issue number replaces '#?' after filing). ORIGINAL TEXT: The read-side scrub scans command_execution (no execution_id index) once per tracker read that has non-empty error text: 38 to 88 ms at 1M rows, 263 to 628 ms at 10M, linear in the table. The reviewer corrected the premise "bounded by the 24 hour reaper": the reaper drains at most about 120,000 rows per day, so above about 1.4 recorded commands per second the table grows without bound and the new scan turns disk growth into read latency; a capped pass is invisible. Native LOW, derived MEDIUM (I5 unbounded growth base). Owner-accepted limit. REVISIT TRIGGER: command_execution live rows above about 1M, or p95 executions-list latency above 200 ms, or a capped correlation reap on three consecutive passes. No-migration mitigations: skip the lookup for a slot already of token shape, add a created_at range predicate on the existing index, cache the immutable "execution is Forensics" fact, and raise or make the reap cap adaptive with a capped-pass alert. Stale comment on the existing alert calls the table lower stakes. No issue filed by this ledger. Also raised as: g8-perf-1 (performance, LOW), g8-arch-7.

summary: CLOSED OUT of this change and carried by Issue 2 (dispatch-record hardening). The work is real and is not done here; it is owed by the follow-up, not by this PR. The remaining work is item(s) of Issue 2 (dispatch-record hardening) in followup-issues-draft-v3.md (the issue number replaces '#?' after filing). ORIGINAL TEXT: MITIGATED, NOT ELIMINATED. In the first form of the g8-up-4 fix the guard compared the persisted text with its sanitised form, which differs for any ordinary free-text failure, so every such frame ran one unindexed scan of command_execution inside the write transaction, holding the agent_exec_status row lock and a lease of the shared 16-connection pool. sre measured it on a disposable PostgreSQL 16 with a 1,000,000-row command_execution on a busy shared host (relative figures only): the lookup alone 32 to 37 ms, the upsert transaction 2.0 ms alone against 118.9 ms with the lookup under 16-way concurrency (about 59 times lower throughput); cpp-safety measured 8.6 ms at 100,000 rows. In 92e0e60f5 (read in the diff) the lookup is skipped whenever the persisted text equals the incoming, already reduced, text, which is every ordinary frame, so each reporter's stated trigger no longer produces the scan. Residuals: a persisted value that differs from the incoming one and is not already a bounded token (the sticky-terminal or older-writer case) still runs one scan inside the write transaction, now savepointed; and the read-side lookup is unchanged, an unindexed scan per tracker read that carries error text, tracked by g8-sre-1 (open, with its revisit trigger). No load run has been made after the change. Row left open so the residual is not read as closed. Mitigated by: fix(tracker): a failed Forensics lookup can no longer lose an agent's status (92e0e60f5). The fix postdates Gate 8 pass 3 and has not been re-reviewed by a governance agent (see gate8-pass4-pending); this row records the claim.

ORIGINAL TEXT: The filtered step collates as pending, so complete stays false and the manifest TTL slides on every poll, so an actively polled bundle is never evicted; an automated worker that follows retry_after_ms loops indefinitely, each poll costing the resolver reads, a collate query and for token callers a denial row. The owner ruled that filtered rows look absent. Mitigation candidates: a hard age cap for a manifest whose steps are terminal at the agent but withheld, a distinct withheld state (needs an owner ruling because of the existence signal), or a poll ceiling in the MCP twin. Documented (REST, MCP, upgrade guide). REVISIT TRIGGER: the shared connection pool saturating under bundle pollers re-derives this to I5(b), HIGH. Also raised as: UP2-1, g8-ch-5 (chaos-injector), g8-hp-2, g8-cons-6. Related change (does not close the finding): docs(rest-api): bundle polling for a caller who cannot read a Forensics step, Console notice (a9feee869); docs(mcp): disclosed exception, reading authority, bundle polling, audit posture difference, troubleshooting (d09bdce5e).
